## HaloBar 0.0.4

### New
- **All apps, the way Start lists them.** The launcher's **All apps** puts everything under its letter, with Start's folders that open in place.
- **App names.** Rest on an app in the dock and its name rises above it in a small pill.
- **Any edge.** The dock can sit at the bottom (centered, from the left or from the right) or on the left or right edge of the screen. Settings → **Position** shows a little monitor with the dock lit where it sits, and the dock moves there live, without the Windows taskbar flashing up in between.
- **Every screen by default**, as the Windows taskbar does. Settings → **Screens** shows your monitors as they stand; pick one for a single dock there.
- **Redesigned settings**, with cards for the theme, size, dock, status, start button and extras.
- **Space widget.** Empty room between widgets, as wide as you drag it. When the dock gets crowded, the spaces give their room back to your apps first.
- **Widgets sized to their words.** Weather, battery and network speed are as wide as what they say, and only shrink back after a quieter spell.
- **Drives widget**, with free space and eject.
- **New right-click menus** in HaloBar's own style, with icons, headers and submenus, for apps, the Windows logo, the recycle bin and the calendar.
- **One opacity with Astraeus.** On the solid looks an opacity slider lets the desktop show through the dock and its panels; following Astraeus, the dock uses Astraeus' own opacity and blur.
- **Win + T and Win + B.** Win + T walks the dock's apps with the arrow keys and Enter, Win + B opens the tray, and Win + 1–9 opens the app in that spot, all as on the Windows taskbar.
- **Drop files on an app.** Drag a file onto an app in the dock to open it there; hold it a moment and the app's window comes up so you can drop straight in.
- **Side dock media pill.** At the side of the screen the song stands as a tall pill with its title turned sideways and the visualizer at its end.
- **Astraeus' fullscreen player.** With Astraeus running, click the album art in the player for its fullscreen player with lyrics; close it and you're back in the player.

### Fixes
- **Tray flyouts open at the right spot**, over their icon in the dock, and apps asking where the taskbar is get the dock's answer.
- **Album covers are more reliable**: art that arrives after the song's name, or the last song's picture left behind, is picked up again.
- **Lighter on the CPU**: a blinking caret no longer redraws its panel all the time, the visualizer's frames skip work they don't need, the glass outline is only sent again when it moves, and the album art's decoded pixels are let go once they're on the screen.

> [!NOTE]
> The executable is not code-signed yet, so Windows SmartScreen may show an "unknown publisher" warning the first time. Click **More info → Run anyway**.
